data: Really good game, chill, and beautiful
I would still recommend it based on the unique mechanics and solid (if easy) puzzle design,
the soundtrack is amazing as well
10/10 art, simplicity, atmosphere, fun, challenging puzzles
An AMAZING game with beautiful visuals and a unique story, as well as so many fun puzzles
the bosses are the worst game design - I wonder who let this through playtesting
It's simply not fun and without character

It's like Tower of Hanoi, if the pieces folded in on themselves and you had to move them across dimensions.

After a fairly unassuming start and middle section that serve as a walkthrough for each separate mechanic, Cocoon becomes truly unique once the player is required to combine mechanics and casually turn the world inside out.
Would love to see the design notes for this one.

This was a mixed experience. There's some good puzzle design here, but the game is weighed down by a surprising number of annoying boss fights. I mean, in a puzzle game any number of boss fights is surprising. There are other less than enjoyable sequences that test reflexes rather than critical thinking. If the game had stuck to what it's good at it would be a lot easier to recommend.

The game is inreadibly nice, I'm so happy I bought it. There is only one interaction button but it doesn't get boring. The riddles are a bit of challenge but not too hard. I play it with my child and we both had a lot of fun already. I like the graphics and athmosphere a lot. Of all the games I bought on Steam Sale this is one of my favourites.

Absolutely brilliant and simple puzzle game. If you liked the mind bending puzzles of Portal, you will enjoy this game. It only uses five keys and there's no dialogue, but this game blends fantastic visuals and a straightforward premise with inception-like gameplay and mind blowing puzzles. I can't imagine what it's like to live in the mind of the creators of this game. How did they come up with this? Absolutely worth your time and money.

One of the best puzzle games I've ever played. Short and sweet. The mechanics are really interesting and figuring out the solutions to the puzzles feels very satisfying. The visauls and soundtrack are really good and add a lot to the experience. I highly recommend this game to fans of puzzle games.
If you need an atmospheric puzzle game that respects your time, you will have a tough time finding a better one than this. I highly recommend to play with headphones.
Beautiful atmospheric and visually wonderful puzzle game! The sound design is fantastic, and the environments are really well designed. Finished in about 4 hours, but it was very memorable!

It's a really fun and quick puzzle game.

It can get pretty trippy at times, but when you work it out, it's worth it. The art and music is pretty cool as well.
Not into puzzle games but this one is a GEM, get it on sale though because it is a very short game

One of the best indie games, 10/10 the art is phenomenal, the puzzles are interesting and make sense, but can be hard at times. The animations for everything is fun to look at, and I never encountered a single bug. Everything just works

I bought this because I was a big fan of Limbo and Inside. While Cocoon is a very pretty game, it's just not very fun. The puzzles are simple and there's only ever one solution. It reminds me a lot of Monument Valley, which was made to play in short burst and very cheap. Another detraction, there is only ever one path to follow. As far as I can tell there's not even hidden collectibles. I had to stop myself from exploring because there was never anything else to find. Story is very abstract/nonexistent. The whole game feels like just solve these puzzles to see the next environment. I finished the first "combat" section and realized this game wasn't worth my time. Better luck next time.

First of all; this isn't your regular game but if your're into puzzles (some were kinda easy but a few took me awhile) beautiful, I mean breathtaking level design, awesome music and sound design then definitely check this game out! it had been on my radar for awhile and after reading a few negative reviews I held off on getting it but after completing it, I wish I hadn't waited so long. basically, I don't think I have a negative word to say about this game. I found it to be one of the coolest, most original games I've had the pleasure of playing. I loved Limbo and Inside and although this is nothing like either of those titles, this one does not disappoint in the slightest IMO.

TLDR: YES, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

It's a great indie puzzle game. It takes that whole "a world in a world in a world" thing and makes great puzzles with it. The length of the game is entirely dependent on your puzzle solving skills, since there is no text or dialogue. It took me 6 hours to beat. I bought in on sale but I think the original 23€ is a bit steep for 6 hours of gameplay.

I've been spoiled by puzzle games. Some triggers the eureka feeling, some blew my mind with world-level meta puzzle, some overheat my brain by the absurd complexity of the solution.

Cocoon never triggered any of those feelings. I never really stumbled on any difficulty, I've mostly been annoyed by the back and forth solutions sometimes required once the problem is revealed. And the feeling that the mechanic hasn't been fully exploited.

You probably can enjoy the games if you just want to see a funny new puzzle mechanic, or if you enjoy its unique artistic design.
Neat mechanics, a little too easy personally, and no where near as good as Inside.

This game has a lot of very unique and interesting puzzle mechanics that enable some really interesting puzzles. The puzzles themselves are also not too difficult, but hard enough that they require some thinking and are quite satisfying when you solve them.
The music in this game is also good, not as great as other soundtracks that I've heard before though. However, it's the visuals that really make it a great game in my opinion. There's a decent amount of visual storytelling, but it leaves a lot of room for interpretation. That's what really made me want to keep playing.
Sadly, you can't keep playing for very long. The game takes only about 4 hours to complete. Therefore, I don't think it should be worth this much money. So you should definitely only buy it when there's a discount.
In conclusion: great game if you have some time to kill and are looking for something casual, but that's about it.

Beautiful game. Stunning artwork, brilliant sound and music. Wonderful design that is engaging and keeps you engaged. Wonderful story as it unfolds, just an all around fun and enjoyable game. I thoroughly enjoyed the experience. Highly recommend.

So fun, until you get to one of the completely unnecessary and random boss fights. For people who like puzzle games (which this is) and hate timing based games and games where it's one-hit-you-die and you have to go back to the very beginning and tediously trudge through the whole fight again.. NOPE.
It's a chill and really awesome puzzle game... and then it's a stupid annoying boss battle.
PLEASE ADD A SKIP BOSS BATTLES FEATURE!!! PLEASE!!!
This was a very fun puzzle game. loved the graphics, gameplay and music. Would 100% recommend.

Too easy for a puzzle game. Only the last 10% feels like a real puzzle game, which still, is on the easy end.
Apart from that, a good game.

Solid game, but is purposely sparse with information. I used a walkthrough a handful of times because the answer to a puzzle was "do a thing for the first time that you didn't know was an option". Otherwise, you can probably figure out 70-80 percent of the game by yourself. But by the end, I was just using a walkthrough because the puzzles went from feeling clever to feeling like busy work, with obvious points of interest really far apart so that you had to keep running back and forth with very little skill involved.

Also the boss fights are bad and tedious because you can fully understand what you are supposed to do/what they want you to do, but then it becomes a game of fast reflexes and executing actions. This is not an action game, and is worse when it tries to be one.
fantastic game. the beauty of reducing everything to core functions with slightly challenging puzzles. pure fun

It's a fun little game!
The mechanics and graphics are absolutely stunning. Easy to understand, cool adventures and plot. The puzzles ain't that difficult in my opinion, but the action and map design is very cool! Probably aimed for a younger audience. Visual clues are also very clear and great for side quests - perfectly possible to accomplish all achievements!

Genre: dungeon-based puzzle

Such a unique puzzle/adventure game. I felt so immersed into the game the whole time, and while a few of the puzzles can be challenging, no part of it was frustrating or tedious, thanks to its short playtime. Amazing music too! 9/10

How is this puzzle even possible? What the heck? Not possible. NOT POSSI...wait. WAIT! OHHHH. AHHHH HAH HAH! I'M A GENIUS!

Repeat.

Cocoon is a fantastically cerebral game that teaches you the language of it's puzzles beautifully through evolving challenges and linking concepts. By the end of the game you will be instinctively building solutions in your mind that are impossible to articulate.
The game and mechanics are also perfectly succinct, not once overstaying their welcome.
If you find yourself early in the game and are concerned that puzzle complexity is tied to juggling a million orbs - stick through it. Cocoon does a great job of introducing new mechanics without being overwhelming.

It's a fun little game. I beat it in 3.5 hours, so I'd definitely get it on sale. I'll admit I found a few things to be a little tedious, like the boss in the purple world. That said, I enjoyed the puzzles and felt pretty smart a few times :)

You should play this game! The puzzles are difficult and evolving enough to always be engaging without ever being so difficult that you ever worry about spending 30 minutes on one puzzle. Short but sweet.
A very fun game with very few buttons, interesting mechanics and a wonderful art style

This game is an absolute treat both visually and audibly, but it unfortunately falls very flat as a puzzle game. The main premise of the game, that of recursion and worlds within worlds, feels strangely underutilized and unincorporated in the vast majority of puzzles. When recursion does come up, the concepts involved are so basic and simplistic that often the player is just doing the next most obvious action with very little critical thinking. By the time the game really starts to do interesting stuff with the recursion mechanics, the game is already over.

I think if you enjoy more linear and streamlined puzzle games like Portal 1 + 2 over more thinky stuff like Baba is You or The Witness, then you might enjoy Cocoon for what it is. For me though, my expectations only led to disappointment.
Perfection. My brain started hurting a little towards the end. It's great. Gorgeous art and really clever mechanics and puzzles. Fun bosses too.

If you've got an afternoon or two to kill, I recommend this game. The puzzles are interesting and the games mechanics allow for some truly lovely problems to solve and *aha* moments to have. Only (very minor) gripe is that there's a lot of walking back and forth between spots, but with this game its kinda how it would work out anyway, but other than that, lovely world, lovely music, and just a good overall vibe. And I finished it in under 5 1/2 hours. 

TLDR: fun short puzzle game, worth the money and the two evenings I spent playing it.

One of the best puzzle games ever made.
The art design is absolutely top-tier. I loved the core mechanic of world-orbs and nesting them inside one another. You never need to look up solutions or guides, if you take your time, you'll figure out everything that initially felt impossible, which makes progress immensely satisfying.
The game is played with just a single button. It reminds me of the saying that true expertise makes complex things look easy, just like an expert dancer or artist makes their craft look effortless, creating a game with no dialogue, no hints, and only one button that still delivers deep puzzles is next-level game design.
While the boss fights are great and many people enjoyed them, my favorite part was the late-game puzzles where you arrange recursive worlds. Plus, the checkpoint load feature makes getting 100% achievements easy.
I absolutely loved this. An incredible game that easily earned a spot among my top favorites.

I didn't find this game particularly difficult. I didn't get stuck very often, and when I did, it only took a bit of thought for me to figure out what I was supposed to do. That said, there were some legitimate mind-bending moments where the game's rules realigned themselves in my mind. 

The game is pretty short, overall, as you can see from my playtime. Not a great deal of replayability, but if you can get it for 10-15 bucks, I'd recommend puzzle-lovers giving it a go.

This is a wonderful puzzle game. It blew my mind several times. The style is minimal and beautiful, and the game-play reflects that. There are no tutorials or text in the game, and yet it's intuitive to play. The difficulty is perfect. I never got stuck, but never felt that the solutions were too obvious.
Mind blowing and creative puzzles, nice ambiance, overall a great game. Also not too long, which I like
Boring waste of time game. The animations are cool, but the game is not fun or challenging

It's a very well designed* short, but full of content puzzle game. It plays very smooth, puts you into the flow. Puzzles are clever so they are interesting, but not hard, so you're never stuck.
However there is a big asterisk on the well designed part. I even contemplated leaving a negative review because of it. There is a section towards the end of the game that drastically differs from the rest of it. This section is unskippable, so to progress you don't have a choice but to suffer through it. It is a timed reflex-based level, despite the rest of the game being a chill classic puzzle. People with disabilities are screwed. I don't understand who the hell thought it was a good idea to change the gameplay so drastically just for this one part. It does not fit in with the rest of the game and it spoiled my enjoyment of it quite a bit.

Unique and creative, with beautiful world desing and soundtrack. The idea of nesting worlds/puzzles is superb and (based on my experience) fresh and innovating. A truly memorable puzzle game, though a bit short and quite easy.
Absolute excellency in puzzle design, atmosphere and presentation. Incredibly clever from begining to end. Not a single bad segment in is whole duration.

Simple mechanics, beautiful graphics, ingenious puzzles, and good music. It's not a long game nor does it have much of a plot, but it doesn't need one. The inception style game play adds a nice twist to the puzzle solving, making you think on multiple levels to solve some of them.

A mind bending, brain melting puzzle game where you hop between the fabric of the universe.

Quite simple and not extremely long. Yet deeply fascinating and interesting. Reeks of Inside in the best ways. Yet also stands on it's own as a wonderful, weird sci-fi adventure.

10/10 Actually made my brain hurt.
A neat little puzzle game that keeps things moving and developing for exactly as long as needed
Not as good as limbo or inside, but still fun. Some puzzles are annoying and repetitive.

Play it.

Going into this game with little context (intentionally avoiding trailers, developer updates, etc) is extremely worth it. At the time of writing this I am probably half way through. The "puzzle" difficulty thus far is perfect, very engaging and challenging, but not enough to be defeating. It is definitely a short game by typical standards but the unique experience makes up for it.

The design and thought behind the game, both visually and technically - has made me drop my jaw multiple times.

This is special.

I played this game a good while ago.
Ngl, I was expecting a puzzle game for sure and for the most part it was fun. I like the idea behind the globes and the me and used, my only problem is , near the end i had the feeling that the devs just kinda made it seem like a drag. I just wanted to end already in the last hour and it got boring quickly. Although if you want a fun and short puzzle experience, check out cocoon it’s fun and it really helps with creativity thinking

I deeply enjoyed the inception and depth of this well-crafted puzzle game. The team did an excellent job introducing the mechanics and guiding the playing gently toward the solution. Each puzzle and fight is immensely satisfying and not too punishing. All around incredible game.

In both style and presentation, COCOON is a stunningly beautiful game. Although it might not be a very long game, it wastes none of your time. Every single moment feels delicately hand-crafted.
The learning curve is quite slow, so the game is unlikely to stump you, making it less of a puzzler and more of a relaxing journey guided by the player's intuition. Nonetheless, the sheer novelty and uniqueness of each puzzle keep them more than satisfying to solve.
To whoever is reading this, I warmly recommend COCOON.

This is a really unique game. It reminds me of some of the puzzle mechanics of Limbo - but the vibe and the level of thinking is different. It's a very enjoyable world to get lost in - and solve - for a while. I have been playing it on and off for weeks now. Worth it if you like puzzling things out whilst exploring alien landscapes. It feels like being a different kind of thing for a while. Fun.

Interesting relationship between levels which can be nested into and taken out of one another, with thoughtful puzzle designs that make use of this novel relationship. A rare and interesting idea with great execution.
Also this game has insanely adorable biomimetic creature designs and cool shaders.

tldr.text: Very Positive (94%): players love the art and the music.
The main complaint is the boss fights, which some players find poorly designed.

details.text: Recent reviews from the last month are slightly less positive than the all-time score, at 91%.
Newer players are far less positive, at 70%, than those who had played a few hours longer, at 95%.
